title: Kummer computations on the line and the punctured line
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $N\geq1$, and put $m=\ell^N$ and $R=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$. Let $A$ be a finite free $R$-module of rank $r\geq0$. Consider the smooth separated affine connected curves $\mathbf A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ and $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-sc-curves], with cohomology on their small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Write $\mu_m(U)=\{u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:u^m=1\}$, an etale sheaf of $R$-modules, and let $A_C$ be the constant sheaf with value $A$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Put $A(1)=\mu_m\otimes_{R_C}A_C$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Choose a primitive $m$-th root of unity $\zeta\in k$.

For every integer $q\geq0$:

1. $H^0(\mathbf A^1_k,A(1))\cong A$ and $H^q(\mathbf A^1_k,A(1))=0$ for $q>0$.
2. $H^0(\mathbf G_{m,k},A(1))\cong A$, and $H^q(\mathbf G_{m,k},A(1))=0$ for $q>1$. In both degree-zero isomorphisms the map from $A$ sends $a$ to the constant section $\zeta\otimes a$; restriction from the affine line to the punctured line corresponds to the identity of $A$.
3. Let $\delta:\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,k},\mathbf G_m)\to H^1(\mathbf G_{m,k},\mu_m)$ be the connecting map for the Kummer sequence [def-sc-kummer-sequence], and put $\kappa_m(t)=\delta(t)$. The $R$-linear map
$$
A\longrightarrow H^1(\mathbf G_{m,k},A(1)),\qquad
 a\longmapsto H^1(i_a)(\kappa_m(t)),\qquad
 i_a:\mu_m\longrightarrow A(1),\quad x\longmapsto x\otimes a,
$$
is an isomorphism. For $A=R$, it sends $1$ to the Kummer generator $\kappa_m(t)$; for general $A$ the group is free of rank $r$ over $R$.

All these cohomology groups are finite $R$-modules. The identifications are natural for $R$-linear maps $A\to B$ of finite free $R$-modules. More explicitly, the coefficient comparison
$$
H^q(C,\mu_m)\otimes_R A\longrightarrow H^q(C,A(1)),\qquad
 x\otimes a\longmapsto H^q(i_a)(x),
$$
is an isomorphism for either curve $C$ and every $q\geq0$. Thus coefficient base change is compatible with the displayed degree-zero sections and Kummer maps: for a finite free commutative $R$-algebra $S$, scalar extension gives $H^q(C,A(1))\otimes_R S\cong H^q(C,\mu_m\otimes_R(A\otimes_R S))$, sending $\kappa_m(t)\otimes a\otimes s$ to the class with coefficient $a\otimes s$.

proof.text: Both curves in the statement are smooth affine connected curves in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. The sheaf $\mu_m$ is torsion: multiplication by $m$ is zero, since each of its sections has $m$-th power one. Apply [lem-sc-affine-cohomological-dimension] to $F=\mu_m$ on each curve to obtain $H^q(C,\mu_m)=0$ for all $q>1$. This uses the affine bound, not a nonexistent affine clause of the general cohomological-dimension node.

proof.text:
Since $m$ is invertible in $k$, [lem-sc-kummer-exact] makes the sequence [def-sc-kummer-sequence] short exact on either curve. The global-sections functor is additive and left exact on the abelian category with enough injectives described by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to this functor and the Kummer sequence. Its degree-zero and degree-one terms give
$$0\to H^0(C,\mu_m)\to\Gamma(C,\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{u\mapsto u^m}\Gamma(C,\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{\delta_C}H^1(C,\mu_m)\to H^1(C,\mathbf G_m).$$
By [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic] the final term is $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, and this is zero on both curves by [lem-pur-affine-punctured-line-algebra]. Consequently $H^0(C,\mu_m)$ is the kernel of the power map and $\delta_C$ induces an isomorphism from its cokernel to $H^1(C,\mu_m)$.

proof.text: Compute the kernels in step 2 using [lem-pur-affine-punctured-line-algebra]. On the affine line the units are $k^\times$, so the kernel is $\mu_m(k)$. On the punctured line every unit has the unique form $a t^e$, with $a\in k^\times$ and $e\in\mathbf Z$; $(at^e)^m=1$ forces $me=0$, hence $e=0$, and then $a^m=1$. Thus both kernels are the same $\mu_m(k)$, with restriction equal to the identity on that group. By [lem-sc-primitive-root], $\zeta$ exists and $R\to\mu_m(k)$, $b\mapsto\zeta^b$, is an isomorphism. This gives the asserted degree-zero maps for coefficients $R$.

source.place: Proof, Degrees 0 and 1, the two kernel calculations; thm-pur-kummer-affine-line proof, H^0 sentence

proof.text: Compute the cokernels in step 2, again using [lem-pur-affine-punctured-line-algebra] with its exponent $N$ specialized to $m$. Every $a\in k^\times$ is an $m$-th power, so the affine-line cokernel is zero, hence $H^1(\mathbf A^1_k,\mu_m)=0$. For the punctured line, $(a,e)\mapsto e\bmod m$ identifies the cokernel with $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$: its kernel consists of $at^{mf}=(bt^f)^m$ after choosing $b^m=a$, and every residue is represented by $t^e$. For $C=\mathbf G_{m,k}$, the inverse of the resulting identification of $H^1(C,\mu_m)$ is $R\to H^1(C,\mu_m)$, $e\mapsto\delta_C(t^e)=e\delta_C(t)$. In particular $1$ maps to $\kappa_m(t)$.

source.place: Proof, Degrees 0 and 1, the two unit quotients and the Kummer class of t

proof.text: Here is the finite-free coefficient argument without an additional field hypothesis. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], a basis $A\cong R^r$ gives $\mu_m\otimes_R A_C\cong\mu_m^{\oplus r}$. With the cohomology model of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], take a nonnegative injective resolution $I^\bullet$ of $\mu_m$. The finite sum $(I^\bullet)^{\oplus r}$ is an injective resolution of $\mu_m^{\oplus r}$: extensions to a finite product of injectives are obtained one component at a time, by the defining extension property in [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and its kernels and images are computed componentwise. Global sections preserve these finite products, so their section complexes and their homology are the corresponding finite sums. This proves that $H^q(C,\mu_m)\otimes_R A\to H^q(C,A(1))$, $x\otimes a\mapsto H^q(i_a)(x)$, is an isomorphism: in a basis it is precisely the sum of the maps from the $r$ summands. Additivity on morphisms follows in the same resolution model by adding lifts of coefficient maps and taking homology. The displayed map is defined without a basis; for $u:A\to B$, $(1\otimes u)i_a=i_{u(a)}$, so functoriality makes it natural in $A$. The empty basis gives zero sheaves and zero cohomology, and is included.

proof.text: Tensor the computations of steps 1, 3 and 4 with $A$ using step 5. The degree-zero generator is $\zeta\otimes a$, the degree-one map on the punctured line is $a\mapsto H^1(i_a)(\kappa_m(t))$, and all other stated groups vanish. The maps in degree zero restrict identically because they are constant sections. Each surviving group is isomorphic to the finite $R$-module $A$, proving finiteness without using a separate finiteness assertion. For finite free $S/R$, both $A$ and $A\otimes_R S$ are finite free over $R$; apply step 5 to each and the associativity isomorphism $(H^q(C,\mu_m)\otimes_R A)\otimes_R S\cong H^q(C,\mu_m)\otimes_R(A\otimes_R S)$. On a pure tensor this is exactly the coefficient comparison in the statement. Naturality from step 5 identifies the sections and the Kummer maps, including $\kappa_m(t)\otimes a\otimes s\mapsto H^1(i_{a\otimes s})(\kappa_m(t))$.
